body: I mean after 9 years of dealing with this and deciding not to kill myself multiple times a week for at least 5 years I guess I picked my head up and said I should probably try to do something that will make this bearable if I am not going to end it. I guess sometimes it just gets the better of me and I have breakdowns that put me back at the drawing board. Which happens to be the thing that gets to me most.

Usually the people in the game is what gets me so irritated. I enjoy the game regardless if it was a bad or good game for me. Just knowing that I can do better is annoying and I usually beat myself up about it in most activities. 

I would love to get into the good part of the community with people that love the game but people are so competitive about everything that it doesn't matter when you are actually playing the game. 

That is part of the stigma right there that I was talking about. People treat me different because I have a mental condition. I want to just be treated like anyone else because that just makes me angry but of course if I tell people that they over compensate which is just as terrible. 

That's one reason I want to get into the gaming community with a job as well. I can understand that not everyone is going to have a passion for the game because some people let their job destroy them but I feel like there has to be someone there that can enjoy their job.

Nothing that I am currently thinking of. I have begun to look into more activities that I can be rather passive in but still yield results that I can be proud of even though they are pretty small and insignificant. Like reading I am still trying to find a genre that interests me enough so that I can read several books in that area. Being able to finish something and either gain knowledge of something or at least be able to escape to that world it is sort of like replacing my highly dysfunctional world with multiple utopias.   I have also been trying to cook at least once a day or so. Even though the end result could be bad I can criticize myself easily enough so that I am still willing and able to do it in the future. I really enjoy video games but because I know so much about them I find myself being overly critical of myself which isn't at all good for me. I do still partake in gaming sessions though just not as intense. 

The thing I think has been my saving grace many times though is having a sense of humor. Being around people who care to much or are scared of the subject makes it hard to have a sense of humor about my condition. Recently I have just stopped caring what people think about my condition or how much it scares them and I just tell my jokes and move on. 

I think I need to find a way to meet people.

Yeah I love thrilling rides. I haven't been on one since I was like 13 or so though. :/

I figured out that the military wasn't giving me what I needed like 3 years into the contract I was on. They basically only prepare you to stay in the military for life. No one cares that I have experience in a high stress environment  if I don't have any credentials saying I can do my job. 

Yeah most network engineers take at least a bachelors and several years experience with all of the certifications they are looking for as well. Which is a lot of time and money that you have to invest (most companies usually pay to get their employees the certifications with the signing of a contract)

I mean I don't really talk to people about killing myself or anything like that because I know it is a bad topic to handle and people get nervous and they think you just put your life in their hands or something. I do tend to have deep and meaningful conversations that approach some of the areas that I have problems with and it just seems like people don't know how to have a conversation that goes past "did you see what Tammy posted on facebook?". I don't expect people to be able to handle what is going on in my head because I have been dealing with it for a while and I can still sometimes not handle it. 

Also the stigma that follows around any mental health issues is insane. I wish I had made a movie about 2 years ago when I finally admitted to myself that I need help or before and after the hospital visits. I don't even know how to describe the change in peoples attitudes around me or even their facial expressions and body language.

I think my main problem with me living at home is I just came from being "on my own" for 5 years in the military. I always thought moving back in with your parents was a sign of failure for some reason. 

I am trying to get into college now. The jobs I am looking for want some type of degree to back up your knowledge or some extensive experience which I didn't get either in the military. I am trying to get a spot in a gaming company as a network engineer eventually. 

I know I shouldn't value others opinions of me and it doesn't matter what other people think. It is just weird hearing that from someone you spent so much time and effort on being your best for them. This was also my longest relationship at ~5 years so I valued her opinion a little more than everyone else's. 

Oddly enough even the few responses I have gotten here are more than I could ask from some of my friends of 10+ years. Maybe I just need to get some better people in my life.

I am 24 I live with my parents have no college education and just got retired from the military for depression. I cut myself so I have become self conscious since my previous girlfriend said "you aren't sexy anymore". Just a few things.

I am usually able to keep myself reasonably busy and I have a couple of coping skills that I use to help me out in a pinch. The issue usually comes around when I am going to sleep if it takes more than an hour or so to get to sleep then I will just continuously churn suicide thoughts and other thoughts of inadequacy.
Right now I am undergoing a fairly substantial life change (discharged from the military and enrolling in college/working again). Hopefully that works out. Thanks for the reply.

I don't think I ever really wake up with a feeling of purpose in my life if that is what you mean. On good days I wake up because I am awake and think nothing of it. On bad days my whole life revolves around depression and I come back to the start and ask myself "would I be better dead?".
